newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol to unveil underground cargo options.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol to unveil underground cargo options.

text.p: Details of a feasibility study looking at an innovative underground cargo transport system will be unveiled at a press conference on Tuesday.

The so-called Underground Logistic System (ULS) has been proposed as a possible means of quickly moving freight to and from the airport to a rail centre at nearby Hoofdorp and a major customer base, the Dutch flower auction at the town of Aalsmeer.

Sources close to the project told Reuters the press conference will include a call by the airport operating company for the Dutch government to take a majority shareholding in the pipeline project, bearing the bulk of construction costs.

In addition, airport officials are expected to unveil some technical proposals for a pilot construction project, as well as details of the proposed dimensions of the ULS' transport tube, the size of pallets, and to release information about a cost benefit analysis which has been underway in recent months.

The ULS may also be proposed as a possible means of quickly moving freight to and from a possible second national airport in the Netherlands, which operating company Amsterdam Airport Schiphol believes could be sited offshore.

The airport operating company last year launched a study looking at three potential new airport options. One was to build an island at an unspecified location in the North Sea; another to reclaim land from the inner reaches of the IJsselmeer, a large, man-made expanse of water near Amsterdam; and a third would be an airport to be built at the mouth of the port of Rotterdam, on a proposed land reclamation site called the Tweede Maasvlakte. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
